summary: Backcountry site near Morice Lake; a Facebook post line gives 1978 with a Nanika Lookout, but no source says what stands there now.

events.note: Facebook group post line reads '1978 Nanika Lookout, via Houston'. The line gives the year only; the post is not confirmed as a photograph.

evidence.supports: Listing gives position 54.137 N, 127.495 W and elevation 1,750 m
Listing puts the site in Bulkley-Nechako
Facebook post line gives 1978 with a Nanika Lookout, via Houston
Nanika Mountain stands at 1,889 m at the northern end of the Morice Range, above the north end of Morice Lake
evidence.quote: Standing at 1889m, Nanika Mountain is located at the northern terminus of the Morice Range and overlooks the north end of Morice Lake.

evidence.supports: Directions give the route as about 80.9 km from Houston
Details block gives the distance from Houston as 60 km or more, which conflicts with the 80.9 km in the directions
Directions start on the Morice River Road
evidence.quote: Head South of town on the Morice River Rd

evidence.supports: Directions continue onto the Morice-West FSR
evidence.quote: After the 44km bridge turn right onto the Morice-West FSR

evidence.supports: Backcountry route for the most advanced and experienced hikers
evidence.quote: Backcountry Route hikes are only for the most advanced and experienced hikers.
There are no directional or trail head signs for this site, use your map and GPS.

evidence.supports: Carry proper gear and emergency provisions
evidence.quote: Never venture out into the back country without proper gear and emergency provisions.

sources.title: Nanika
sources.publisher: Canada Lookouts (Canada's Fire Lookouts, Ron Kemnow)

notes_for_editor: Three sources only. The Facebook post could be read only as one line of text (the page returned little else), so the 1978 year rests on that line alone and the post is not confirmed as a photograph. Nothing in the sources gives a build date, builder, design, staffing or status. The listing's 1,750 m and the Houston Hikers height of 1,889 m for Nanika Mountain may describe different points; the sources do not say whether the lookout stood on that peak. The Houston Hikers page gives two distances from Houston (80.9 km in its directions, 60 km or more in its details) and does not mention a lookout at all. The Canada Lookouts listing gives coordinates without N or W letters; the hemispheres are read from the region. The land status is not stated, so no access level is recorded. 'FSR' is read here as forest service road, as is usual in BC.
